spans.claim: Sir Charles Vandrift is the victim of repeated deception
spans.anchor: we've just been done jolly well brown
spans.span: I say, Sey, my boy, we've just been done jolly well brown, haven't we?

spans.claim: Colonel Clay is a master of disguise and deception
spans.anchor: he appears to possess an india-rubber face
spans.span: He is a Colonel, because he occasionally gives himself a commission; he is called Colonel Clay, because he appears to possess an india-rubber face, and he can mould it like clay in the hands of the potter.

spans.claim: Madame Picardet is an accomplice of Colonel Clay
spans.anchor: she and they spoke to you about him

spans.claim: The forged cheque was signed by Sir Charles Vandrift
spans.anchor: a cheque to Self or Bearer, for 5000 pounds, signed by Sir Charles
spans.span: It lay in a cheque to Self or Bearer, for 5000 pounds, signed by Sir Charles, and evidently paid across the counter in London, as it bore on its face no stamp or indication of any other office.

spans.claim: Colonel Clay uses multiple aliases and disguises
spans.anchor: Senor Antonio Herrera, alias the Reverend Richard Peploe Brabazon
spans.span: You are--Colonel Clay, alias Senor Antonio Herrera, alias the Reverend Richard Peploe Brabazon.

spans.claim: Medhurst is actually Colonel Clay in disguise
spans.anchor: I will lay my plans deep, and I hope before long to secure him
spans.span: But I will lay my plans deep, and I hope before long to secure him.

spans.claim: Dolly Lingfield took photographs revealing Colonel Clay's true face
spans.anchor: one of his peculiar photographs taken by Dolly Lingfield

spans.claim: Dr. Beddersley uses photographic analysis to reconstruct the true face
spans.anchor: I think I can point out certain details in common

spans.claim: Paul Finglemore is the true identity of Colonel Clay
spans.anchor: Paul Finglemore, otherwise Cuthbert Clay, I arrest you

spans.claim: The trial at the Old Bailey results in conviction
spans.anchor: We find him guilty on all the counts of the indictment

spans.claim: The dispatch-box was stolen and returned by Madame Picardet
spans.anchor: I return your dispatch-box intact, with the papers untouched

spans.claim: The ring with a tiny mirror was used to cheat at cards
spans.anchor: an extremely tiny convex mirror... he held this hand carelessly

spans.claim: The real Reverend Brabazon appears in court, shaking identification
spans.anchor: Look at that gentleman! The Reverend Richard Brabazon

spans.claim: Charles Vandrift's credibility is undermined by his own admissions
spans.anchor: Sir Charles Vandrift's obvious dishonesty

spans.claim: Cesarine is an accomplice and lover of Colonel Clay
spans.anchor: Cesarine has long been accomplices

spans.claim: Medhurst's reports are self-serving and misleading
spans.anchor: Medhurst promised to comply... I'll spot him

spans.claim: The fake diamonds were used as a lure in the swindle
spans.anchor: They were only paste--very wonderful paste

spans.claim: Colonel Clay's letter admits partial remorse but continues deception
spans.anchor: Yours, with a tinge of penitence, but still a rogue
spans.span: Yours, with a tinge of penitence, but still a rogue, CUTHBERT CLAY.

spans.claim: The final sentence of Paul Finglemore is fourteen years' imprisonment
spans.anchor: I sentence you to Fourteen Years' Imprisonment, with Hard Labour
spans.span: I sentence you to Fourteen Years' Imprisonment, with Hard Labour.

spans.claim: The composite face reveals the underlying true identity
spans.anchor: a tolerably correct idea of what the actual man himself looks like
spans.span: I _think_ by that time--putting two and two together--I can eliminate the false and build up for you a tolerably correct idea of what the actual man himself looks like.
